records.question: Which federal bodies are on the government's own books, and which sit outside?
records.answer: Of the 352 bodies on the federal tree (committees counted separately), 271 are counted in the government's own audited statements. 26 are disclosed but kept off the books (Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, Amtrak, The Federal Reserve System), 13 are related parties the U.S. influences but does not control (Federal Home Loan Banks, IMF, IBRD), and 33 sit outside (Farm Credit System, Brand USA, In-Q-Tel); 9 have no placement yet. The test is the federal accounting standard SFFAS 47. The 25 Reserve Bank branch offices are listed too and counted with their Reserve Bank; Buffalo is closed but stays listed.

records.question: Which federal agencies does each executive order put to work?
records.answer: The 509 Trump executive orders with agency maps (January 20, 2017 to September 29, 2026) put 163 federal agencies and offices to work. The Justice Department is named in the most orders (153), then the Office of Management and Budget (147) and the Department of Homeland Security (139).

records.question: What has each congressional committee actually done in the 119th Congress, and which committees were never checked?
records.answer: The library tracks 226 congressional committees and subcommittees of the 119th Congress. It has checked the calendars of 32; 194 were never checked, so a blank for them means not looked at, not idle. It holds 276 dated, officially verified outcomes for 19 of them (bills marked up, reported or passed, nominations, subpoenas and released transcripts), most from Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (101). The newest is from July 22, 2026.

records.question: Which advisory boards, research centers and councils belong to, or advise, which federal agency?
records.answer: The library has 102 checked relationships for 42 boards, councils and research centers across 28 agencies or offices. 19 are federally funded research centers, all run day to day by private operators (MITRE Corporation 6, RAND Corporation 4, Institute for Defense Analyses (IDA) 3); the rest are boards and councils that advise or are set up inside an agency. Being sponsored or supported is not being owned or controlled.

records.question: Which parts of the national fraud-detection system are proven, and which are only announced or missing?
records.answer: Of the 33 parts of the national fraud-detection system the library mapped, 18 are proved by a public record, 7 are announced with no public text, 2 are proposed and 2 are the library's inference. 4 are missing: Technical annex / SLA, NFDC system records, Collected recovery and Correction, notice and remedy path. Since the map, Treasury reported pre-payment verification fully operating on September 30, 2026.

records.question: Which Supreme Court money-case dates are coming up?
records.answer: 7 dates are set across the 5 live Supreme Court money cases; the next is October 23, 2026 (DHS v. D.V.D.: Government merits brief due). 5 of them are not on the library's waiting list yet. Custodia's October 28, 2026 date is the library's scheduling inference, not a court date.

records.question: What were the White House economists arguing, and which papers matter now?
records.answer: The library saved 26 Council of Economic Advisers papers, from April 3, 2025 to July 15, 2026. 7 are flagged Immediate (Measuring Balance of Payments Deficits; Savings from Most-Favored-Nation Drug Pricing Policy; Effects of Stablecoin Yield Prohibition on Bank Lending; Estimating the Cost of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to Consumers; Artificial Intelligence and the Great Divergence; Retail Access to Alternative Investments Via Defined Contribution Plans; The Economic Benefits of Current Deregulatory Efforts), 10 are routed to a storyline and 9 are kept for reference. Nothing has been checked since July 21, 2026.

records.question: What has our research already answered, and as of when?
records.answer: The library holds 223 saved studies, each with a one-line answer and the date its evidence runs through: 210 current and 13 archived. By that date, 56 run through October 2026, 82 run through September 2026, 38 run through August 2026 and 47 through July 2026. The oldest answer is current to July 13, 2026; the newest, “Fed Standing Repo Central Clearing Proposal,” to October 22, 2026. The biggest rooms are Banking & the Dollar (43), Crypto & Digital Money (36), Government Changes (36). An answer holds only as of its own date.

records.question: Which federal changes has the research found but not yet written up as recorded changes?
records.answer: 18 federal changes, dated September 17, 2026 to September 22, 2026, have been researched with a before and after and an official source but are not yet written up in the movement registry. Among them: FY2026 standardized rating and performance-award controls (Office of Personnel Management); Polysilicon anti-stockpiling import gate (Bureau of Industry and Security); Fort Carson and Pinon Canyon withdrawal extension PLO 7971 (Bureau of Land Management); Temporary moratorium on certain ACA Marketplace agent and broker registration (Department of Health and Human Services and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services). The research accepted all 18; each card prints its review decision and what the record does not prove.

records.question: What is the library waiting on, and when is it due?
records.answer: The library is waiting on 206 open questions. 98 have a date to look again: 8 are past due and 20 fall in the next two weeks. The other 108 wait for a named event, filing or ruling.
